title: The scams Nigerians meet most, and the safe response to each

say: The scams Nigerians meet most, and the safe response to each.
This is the video for module two: common scams in Nigeria and how each one works.
The most common scams do not ask for a huge sum. Someone pretends to be your bank, your network or a government office, and asks for one small thing: a code.
Your account number is fine to share. People need it to pay you.

panel.heading: What you may share, and what you never share

say: But your bank will never call, SMS, email or WhatsApp you for your PIN, password, OTP, full card details or BVN. Anyone who asks is a scammer, no matter how much they know about you.

panel.heading: What you may share, and what you never share

say: A polite customer care agent says your BVN is suspended, and talks you through reactivation.

You read it aloud. Money leaves

say: While he talks, he is trying to log in to your account, or add his phone as a new device.

say: When you read it out, you approve his access. So never read out a code. CBN, EFCC and NCC staff do not phone people to collect fees or codes either.

say: A Ponzi scheme pays early members with newer members' money. When new money slows, it freezes withdrawals and collapses. Chioma does the sums first.

card.title: What 30% a month would really mean
card.note: No legitimate business grows money like this.

say: 100,000 naira at 30% becomes 130,000 after 1 month.

card.title: What 30% a month would really mean
card.note: No legitimate business grows money like this.

say: About 482,700 after 6 months, and about 54 million after 24 months.
No real business can do that. Banks and listed companies earn far less, and their returns go up and down. So Chioma declines.

say: Check the company on the SEC Nigeria website, and banks on the CBN website. A CAC registration only means the business exists.
A balance growing on an app screen is not money in your account. And never pay extra to unlock what you are owed.

panel.heading: Check any investment offer
items: Guaranteed high returns, no risk? Walk away
Bonuses for recruiting friends? Walk away
Check SEC Nigeria at sec.gov.ng
CAC registration is not permission to invest
Never pay fees to release your own money

say: Task jobs that pay you to like videos often ask for a deposit to unlock bigger tasks. Real employers do not charge you to get a job.

panel.heading: Three more scams and the safe response

cards.d: Real employers never ask you to pay a registration, training, medical or visa fee to get a job.
Insist on pay on delivery, or a live video of the item with today's date beside it.
Only your line shows No service? From another phone, call your network, then your bank.

say: Zainab in Kano saw a blender for 28,000 naira, far below the shops. The vendor refused pay on delivery, the account name did not match, and he sent a stock photo instead of a dated video. She did not pay.

say: If your line suddenly shows No service while others have signal, act fast. Call your network to block the number, then your bank to freeze transfers. Set a SIM PIN and turn on WhatsApp two-step verification.

say: To remember. Never share a code. Only your app balance proves money arrived. No live video plus a crisis means scam.
Guaranteed high returns are impossible. And never pay to get a job.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Never share PIN, OTP, password, card details or BVN
Only your app balance proves money arrived
No live video call plus a money crisis means scam
Guaranteed high monthly returns are impossible
Never pay to get a job; pay on delivery when new
